title: Kung Pao Chicken
subtitle: Sichuan stir-fried chicken with peanuts and dried chillies
excerpt: Kung pao chicken (gong bao ji ding) is a Sichuan stir-fry of cubed chicken, roasted peanuts, dried chillies, and Sichuan pepper in a sharp, lightly sweet sauce. The numbing tingle of Sichuan pepper and the searing heat of the dried chillies are both characteristic of the dish.
sourceNotes: Kung pao chicken is named after Ding Baozhen, a Qing Dynasty official with the title Gong Bao (Palace Guardian). The dish originated in Sichuan province and uses the classic Sichuanese combination of dried chillies and Sichuan pepper for the 'mala' (numbing and spicy) flavour profile.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce and marinade can be prepared up to 1 day ahead.

content.text: The hallmark of good kung pao chicken is the contrast of textures: tender, velvetised chicken against the crunch of peanuts. The chicken is marinated in soy sauce and cornflour (a technique called velveting), which keeps it tender in the high-heat wok. Work fast: everything happens in under 3 minutes once the wok is hot.

items.prepNote: 2 tbsp for marinade, 2 tbsp for sauce
1 tbsp for marinade, 1 tbsp for sauce slurry

content.text: Marinate the chicken: mix with 2 tablespoons soy sauce and 1 tablespoon cornflour. Leave for 15 minutes. Make the sauce: mix 2 tablespoons soy sauce, the rice vinegar, sugar, and 1 tablespoon cornflour with 3 tablespoons water. Set aside.
Heat the wok over the highest heat until smoking. Add 2 tablespoons of the sunflower oil. Stir-fry the chicken in batches for 2 to 3 minutes until golden. Remove.

Add the remaining oil. Add the dried chillies and Sichuan pepper and stir-fry for 20 seconds until fragrant and the chillies begin to darken. Add the garlic, ginger, and spring onion. Stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken to the wok. Pour in the sauce and toss to coat. Add the peanuts and toss. Drizzle with sesame oil and serve immediately with steamed rice.

items.symptom: Chicken is chewy and grey rather than tender and golden
items.cause: Wok was not hot enough, or too much chicken was cooked at once. The chicken steamed rather than stir-fried
items.fix: Cook the chicken in two batches, not all at once. The wok must be smoking before each batch goes in.
